subject: Problems with my model using the graded reponse model

messages.author: 9591e6dc05512e96
messages.subject: Problems with my model using the graded reponse model
parts:
HI, I'm actually using a multidimensionnal graded response model to assess a parenting scale( type Likert), everything seems fine except that the expected score, when related to both Theta, seems inverted. As an example, I would expect a respondent with low ability levels on both factors to respond 1 or 2, but all of my items, based on the estimated parameters, show that someone with a low ability level should respond 5. Also, the item fit is fairly bad ranging from -94 to 3, while the RMSEA, TLI and CFI are ok.

This the code I used, mmod1 <- mirt(w, 2, itemtype="graded", SE=TRUE, SE.type = "MHRM", method = "MHRM", optimizer = "NR", calcNull = TRUE, draws = 5000)

N=480, no missing data

Could someone tell me what I'm doing wrong?

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Problems with my model using the graded reponse model
parts:
This is an exploratory model, so I'm not sure what you mean when you are referring to the expected test score function (the function is subject to rotation, which may arbitrarily have negative loadings, and therefore can take on different orientations). You could try passing different rotations to the respective functions, but I generally think that if you have a good idea of what the structure should be you should change to a confirmatory model to avoid problems like this. In which case, you'll have to specify the factor loadings explicitly though a mirt.model() definition. Hope that helps.

Phil
